description: Roman settlement that is potentially part of the same settlement as Bourton-on-the-water, occupation date is suggested to be late 2nd - early 5th CE. Religious features were discovered in a well-deposit such as sculpture and altars, leading to the suggestion that a shrine may be on the site. Though given the proximity to Bourton-on-the-water this may very well have come from the structure identified there.
bibliography: Allen, Martyn, Tom Brindle, Alex Smith, Julian D Richards, Tim Evans, Neil Holbrook, Michael Fulford, and Nathan Blick. “The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: An Online Resource.” Archaeology Data Service, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.

Timby, Jane R., and Jane Timby. Excavations at Kingscote and Wycomb, Gloucestershire: A Roman Estate Centre and Small Town in the Cotswolds with Notes on Related Settlements. Cirencester: Cotswold Archaeological Trust, 1998.
